Without Einstein, the colour gold would be silver.
Almost every metal is silvery grey. Gold is one of the very few that isn't.
Gold's nucleus has seventy-nine protons. They whip its innermost electrons around at about fifty-eight percent of the speed of light.
At that speed, relativity kicks in. The electrons act heavier, and their orbits shrink.
That shift lets gold absorb blue light. Silver only absorbs ultraviolet, which we can't see.
Take blue out of white light, and what's left looks yellow. ~That's gold.
Without relativity, gold would reflect every colour, just like silver.
So every gold ring you've ever seen is a little piece of relativity.
